s1.syndrome_frame: Acute left flank pain with purpuric patch and vascular history
salient_findings: Left flank pain of 1 week's duration
Purpuric patch with a darker stellate patch within it
History of severe peripheral arterial disease and ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
Left flank pain duration is 1 week
Purpuric patch is well-defined and measures 5 × 12-cm
Patient has a history of severe peripheral arterial disease
Patient has a remote history of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
Patient underwent percutaneous endovascular stenting of a left popliteal artery aneurysm 3 months prior to presentation
Biopsy findings show needle-shaped clefts within the lumen of a blood vessel with minimal perivascular inflammation
Biopsy findings show eccrine ducts with cellular dyshesion and necrosis
CT of abdomen and pelvis shows no intraperitoneal or retroperitoneal hemorrhages
CT angiography reveals occluded bilateral common, internal, and external iliac arteries
C-reactive protein is elevated at 57.50 mg/L
Peripheral eosinophil count, creatinine level, and urinalysis are within normal limits

differentials: Hypercoagulable state due to factor V Leiden mutation
per_call: Hypercoagulable state due to factor V Leiden mutation

shortlist.label: Cholesterol crystal embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of severe peripheral arterial disease and recent vascular procedure, which increases the risk of cholesterol crystal embolism

shortlist.label: Atheroembolism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age, history of peripheral arterial disease, and presence of purpuric patch are consistent with atheroembolism

shortlist.label: Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein and presence of purpuric patch with biopsy findings of needle-shaped clefts within the lumen of a blood vessel suggest vasculitis

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of vascular events and presence of purpuric patch could be consistent with antiphospholipid syndrome

shortlist.label: Livedoid vasculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with purpuric patch and history of vascular disease could be consistent with livedoid vasculopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's history of severe peripheral arterial disease, remote history of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm, and recent percutaneous endovascular stenting procedure increase the risk of atheroembolism. The biopsy findings of needle-shaped clefts within the lumen of a blood vessel with minimal perivascular inflammation are consistent with atheroembolism. The presence of a purpuric patch and elevated C-reactive protein also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cholesterol crystal embolism
rejected.why: While similar to atheroembolism, the biopsy findings and clinical presentation do not specifically suggest cholesterol crystal embolism.

rejected.label: Vasculitis
rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show significant perivascular inflammation, which is typically seen in vasculitis.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of antiphospholipid antibodies or other characteristic features of this syndrome.

rejected.label: Livedoid vasculopathy
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match the typical characteristics of livedoid vasculopathy.
